title: Knowledge Subsumption and Computational Reorganization
hypothesis: Cumulative experience can replace memorizing computation with a reusable generalizing circuit while preserving previously acquired behavior.

scope.claim_limit: This experiment tests representational reorganization. A positive result is not evidence that MiniCells uniquely causes grokking or that structural growth is necessary.

task.control_definition: A deterministic random commutative mapping with exactly modulus ordered examples per class; label(a,b)=label(b,a), so the negative control respects the model's exact input symmetry while removing the modular-addition rule.

model.cell_definition: fixed contiguous hidden-neuron groups used only for causal ablation

causal_probe.key_frequency_selection: top conjugate Fourier-frequency pairs by late embedding energy; DC excluded from ranking and retained in restricted/excluded filters

interpretation_limits: A fact is not assumed to map one-to-one to a cell.
Behavioral retention is required; preserving historical internal representations is not.
Fourier restricted/excluded evaluation operationalizes circuit formation and cleanup for modular addition; it is task-specific evidence, not a universal definition of knowledge.
Cell-path reuse is reported as a secondary causal diagnostic and is not part of the formal pass/fail gate.
The random-label control preserves the model's commutative input symmetry and exact class balance, so a negative control result cannot be explained by an unrepresentable asymmetric target.
Every random-label control must itself satisfy the memorization-validity requirement; an unlearned control invalidates the experiment rather than counting as a successful negative control.
The balanced-random-label arm must not produce a false positive under the same gate.
The oracle arm is descriptive and is not part of the pass/fail gate.
Failure rejects this frozen v1 mechanism test; it does not prove that all possible neural systems can never reorganize knowledge.
